﴿وَكَمْ مِنْ مَلَكٍ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ لا تُغْنِي شَفَاعَتُهُمْ شَيْئًا إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ أَنْ يَأْذَنَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَرْضَى﴾ [An-Najm: 26] ﴿And how many an angel there is in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all, except after Allah gives permission to whom He wills and approves.﴾

﴿كَمْ﴾ is *takthiriyyah* (كم تكثيرية, the "many" use of kam), because it is used in that sense; that is, "many." It also comes as *istifhamiyyah* (كم استفهامية, the interrogative use), as when you say to someone: "كم مالك؟" ("How much is your wealth?"). In the words of Allah, Exalted: ﴿وَكَمْ قَصَمْنَا مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ كَانَتْ ظَالِمَةً﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 11] ﴿How many a town We have destroyed, which had been wrongdoing⁠—﴾, it is takthiriyyah. Here, ﴿وَكَمْ مِنْ مَلَكٍ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ﴾ means: many angels are in the heavens. ﴿لا تُغْنِي شَفَاعَتُهُمْ﴾ ("whose intercession will not avail"). Here He says ﴿كَمْ مِنْ مَلَكٍ﴾ ("how many an angel"), and how noble the angels are, as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿بَلْ عِبَادٌ مُكْرَمُونَ﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 26] ﴿Rather, they are honored servants.﴾

﴿فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ﴾ ("in the heavens") and not on the earth, and the heavens are higher than the earth. If these noble angels, whose abode is the heavens (except for one who has been permitted to descend to the earth), have intercession that does not benefit, can the intercession of al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat benefit? The answer is no. That is, it is as if Allah is saying to them: these idols of yours, which you seek intercession through with Allah, ﴿كَمْ مِنْ مَلَكٍ﴾ ("how many an angel"), who is more noble than these idols, ﴿فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ﴾ ("in the heavens"), which are more noble than the earth, ﴿لا تُغْنِي شَفَاعَتُهُمْ شَيْئًا﴾ ("whose intercession will not avail at all"). Even if they interceded, it would not avail, except with two conditions: ﴿إِلَّا أَنْ يَأْذَنَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ ("except that Allah gives permission to whom He wills") from among the angels to intercede, so he intercedes, ﴿وَيَرْضَى﴾ ("and approves"), that is, He approves of the one for whom intercession is made, and likewise of the intercessor, because He cannot permit the intercessor except after He is pleased with him, and He must be pleased with the one for whom intercession is made. Otherwise, intercession does not benefit, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿وَلا يَشْفَعُونَ إِلَّا لِمَنِ ارْتَضَى﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 28] ﴿And they do not intercede except for one whom He approves.﴾ So these idols of yours will not benefit you, and Allah will not accept their intercession.

The conditions of intercession are now three. The first: Allah's approval of the intercessor, by his being qualified for intercession through being one of those brought near to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The second: that He approves of the one for whom intercession is made, by his being qualified to be interceded for. As for the disbelievers, ﴿فَمَا تَنْفَعُهُمْ شَفَاعَةُ الشَّافِعِينَ﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 48] ﴿so the intercession of the intercessors will not benefit them.﴾

The third: permission, due to the words of Allah, Exalted: ﴿مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِنْدَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 255] ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾

So there must be three conditions: Allah's approval of the intercessor, His approval of the one for whom intercession is made, and His permission for the intercession.

﴿وَكَمْ مِنْ مَلَكٍ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ لا تُغْنِي شَفَاعَتُهُمْ شَيْئًا إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ أَنْ يَأْذَنَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَرْضَى﴾ In this verse is a despairing of these polytheists regarding the intercession of their gods on their behalf.

The commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 53, verse 27:

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter name the angels with the names of females.﴾ [An-Najm 27] Allah emphasized this report with His words: ﴿Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter [will] name...﴾. He emphasized it with two emphatic particles, namely: ﴿Indeed﴾ (inna) and the lam (la-).

The meaning of ﴿do not believe in the Hereafter﴾ is that they do not affirm it, nor what it contains of reward and punishment. For belief in the Hereafter must include belief that this Day will come to pass, and belief in everything that has been established as occurring in it and taking place within it, whether in the Qur'an or in the Sunnah. So much so that Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, said: among what falls under belief in Allah and the Last Day is belief in what occurs after death, namely the trial of the grave (fitnat al-qabr), the punishment of the grave ('adhab al-qabr), and the bliss of the grave (na'im al-qabr).

He, may Allah have mercy on him, spoke the truth. For when a person dies, his resurrection (qiyamah) has come: he has ended from the world as though he had never been. Just as there came upon man a span of time when he was nothing worthy of mention, so there will come upon him a span of time when he will be nothing but a report among reports. As the wise poet said about this world:

"While a man is seen in it as one who gives news, ∗∗∗ until he is seen as a report among reports."

You now speak, saying: such-and-such happened, and such-and-such happened; and so-and-so said such-and-such. On some day, about you it will be reported: so-and-so said such-and-such, and you are dust (rameem).

So belief in the Hereafter includes belief in the occurrence of the Last Day, and that it will certainly come.

Second: belief in what will happen on that Day of terrors, reckoning, scales, the bridge (sirat), Paradise and Hellfire. This is necessary.

Likewise, belief in the Hereafter includes belief in what occurs in the grave, namely the trial of the grave, which is—I mean the trial of the grave—the two angels questioning the deceased about three things: Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your Prophet?

﴿Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter﴾: Are there people who do not believe in the Hereafter? Yes, many people do; most people do not believe in the Hereafter. So much so that Allah, glorified and exalted, said about man: ﴿Does man not see that We created him from a drop of semen, and then he is an open adversary? And he presents for Us an example and forgets his [own] creation. He says, "Who will give life to bones while they are decayed?"﴾ [Ya-Sin 77-78]. How excellent is His saying ﴿and forgets his creation﴾ before this man makes his statement; meaning, this man said: ﴿Who will give life to bones while they are decayed?﴾ and ﴿forgets his creation﴾. What is his creation? That he was nothing; ﴿created from a fluid ejected﴾ [At-Tariq 6], then he became bones, sinews and flesh, and became a human being who speaks and argues. ﴿He says, "Who will give life to bones while they are decayed?" Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knowing of all creation."﴾ [Ya-Sin 78, 79]. He also mentioned the proofs for the possibility of that.

The point is that among people there are those who deny the Last Day, saying: there is no resurrection. This is from foolishness in intellect and misguidance in religion. For is it within wisdom that this creation should be created, tested with commands and prohibitions, engage in jihad and fighting enemies, and make lawful their blood, wealth and women, and then the outcome be nothing? This is impossible; wisdom utterly rejects it. Therefore those who do not believe in the Hereafter are foolish in intellect and misguided in religion.

﴿They name the angels with the names of females﴾ [An-Najm 27]: meaning they make the angels females, like the polytheists, who said: the angels are the daughters of Allah. So they named the angels with the naming of females, which is daughters; because they do not believe in the Hereafter. Had they believed in punishment, they would not have said this, but they do not believe, so they say what they wish.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And they have no knowledge of it.﴾ [An-Najm 28] He negates that they have any knowledge of this, because that is the reality. Did they witness the creation of the angels? No. For this reason Allah says in another verse: ﴿And they made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females. Did they witness their creation?﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 19] The answer is no. But: ﴿Their testimony will be recorded and they will be questioned﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 19], when they will find no answer. These people who said "the angels are daughters of Allah" — He, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿they have no knowledge of it﴾ [An-Najm 28]. The word ﴿ilm﴾ (knowledge) here is in the genitive case because of the preposition, and the preposition here, according to the grammarians, in ﴿they have no knowledge of it﴾ [An-Najm 28], is a superfluous (ziyadah) preposition. Its purpose is to emphasize the negation. For this reason we give you a useful rule: all superfluous particles are intended for emphasis; they are among the tools of emphasis. Every superfluous particle, whether the bāʾ, the lām or others, conveys emphasis. ﴿They have no knowledge of it﴾ [An-Najm 28] means: neither a little nor a lot, because they did not witness their creation.

﴿They follow nothing but conjecture (ẓann)﴾. Here "in" (in) means "mā" (not). The rule is that when "illā" (except) comes after "in," it carries the meaning of "mā." For example: ﴿in hādhā illā basharun﴾, meaning: this is nothing but a human being. ﴿in hādhā illā malakun karīm﴾ [Yusuf 31], meaning: this is nothing but a noble angel. ﴿in antum illā basharun mithlunā﴾ [Ibrahim 10], meaning: you are nothing but humans like us. ﴿in hum illā yaẓunnūn﴾ [Al-Jathiyah 24], meaning: they do nothing but conjecture. Examples of this are numerous.

﴿They follow nothing but conjecture﴾ means they follow nothing but ẓann, and by ẓann here is meant a false delusion, not the stronger of two probabilities.

Pay attention to this point: ẓann (conjecture/assumption) comes with three meanings: accusation (tuhmah), the preponderance of something (rujḥān al-shay'), and certainty (yaqīn). How many is that, brother? Three.

The meaning of accusation is the first; the second is preponderance; the third is certainty. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿those who think (yaẓunnūna) that they will meet their Lord﴾ [Al-Baqarah 46], meaning certainty. In the Hereafter, conjecture is not sufficient; one must be certain. The Prophet ﷺ said: «If one of you doubts in his prayer, let him seek out what is correct» [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (401) and Muslim (572/89), from the hadith of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd radiyallahu ʿanhu]. Here "taḥarrī" means the dominant conjecture. And here ﴿in hum illā yaẓunnūn﴾ [Al-Jathiyah 24] is the ẓann of accusation; that is, they think a thought that is delusion with no basis.

Some scholars derived from this verse that it is impermissible to act upon ẓann in legal matters and others, and this is an error, because many legal matters are based on ẓann, either because the evidence is obscure or its indication is obscure. Not every matter of jurisprudence that a person affirms is affirmed with absolute certainty; rather some of it is certain and some of it is ẓann, and ẓann, when certainty is unattainable, is among what Allah has permitted.

And praise be to Allah, it is among the blessings of Allah that when certainty is unattainable we return to the dominant conjecture. Not every ẓann is blameworthy, but the ẓann that has no basis on which to be built, that is what is condemned. Those who named the angels with the name of females, do they have any knowledge of this? Not at all. It is a conjecture founded on delusion, and perhaps founded on desire; that is, it never occurred to them that they were females, but they followed their fathers.

﴿And indeed conjecture avails nothing against the truth﴾. Which conjecture is this? The one founded on delusion, not on indicators. ﴿It avails nothing against the truth﴾ means it does not benefit in the least regarding the truth, because it is a false delusion, and a false delusion can never benefit.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿So turn away from those who turn away from Our reminder and desire nothing but the worldly life﴾ [An-Najm 29]. The address ("turn away") is directed to the Messenger ﷺ, or it may mean every person to whom address can be directed. On the first view the meaning is: "Turn away, O Muhammad." On the second: "Turn away, O believing person."

﴿Turn away from those who turn away from Our reminder and desire nothing but the worldly life﴾: that is, turn away from him, do not follow him, and do not let his affair concern you. The meaning is not "turn away from him and do not advise him." No! Reminding is obligatory. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And remind, for indeed the reminder benefits the believers﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat 55]. That is, remind everyone; some people benefit and some do not, and the one who benefits is the believer. Accordingly we say: the meaning of "turn away" here is: do not be concerned with him, do not let his affair trouble you, do not grow weary because of his turning away, but call to the path of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, whoever he may be. Yet whoever turns away and withdraws, do not let his affair concern you.

﴿Turn away from those who turn away from Our reminder﴾: this is the Qur'an. It may also be that "reminder" means "admonition," i.e., "from Our admonition," and both meanings are valid and interrelated. ﴿So turn away from those who turn away from Our reminder﴾ means away from the Qur'an, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And indeed it is a reminder for you and for your people﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 44], and He says: ﴿It is only a reminder and a clear Qur'an﴾ [Ya-Sin 69]. Or the meaning is: ﴿from Our reminder﴾, that is, from Our admonition with the exhortations that Allah the Mighty and Majestic sends down.

﴿And desire nothing but the worldly life﴾: O Allah, protect us from the trial of this world. That is, he does not desire the Hereafter and has no concern for it; his whole concern is this world: what mount he rides, what clothing he wears, what dwelling he occupies, whom he marries. ﴿They followed what they were given of luxury therein, and they were criminals﴾. He does not care about the Hereafter; the most important thing to him is this world. As for the remembrance of Allah, the Qur'an, or the admonition of Allah, he turns away from it, and we seek refuge with Allah. We ask Allah for safety and well-being.

﴿So turn away from those who turn away from Our reminder and desire nothing but the worldly life﴾. But look at ﴿the worldly life﴾: it is described as "worldly" (dunya) from "dana," meaning near, because of the lowness of its rank and because it comes before the Hereafter. For the worldly abode is the first abode a person dwells in, and it precedes the Hereafter in time. So it is "dunya," that is, near, and it is also "dunya" in terms of rank: it is nothing compared to the Hereafter. This is why the Prophet ﷺ said, in what is authentically reported from him: «The place of one of your whips in Paradise is better than the world and all that is in it» [Reported by al-Bukhari (2892) from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, may Allah be pleased with him]. O Allah, make for us a place in it, better than the world and all that is in it. It is not better than only the world you are in now, but better than the world from the time Allah created it until it perishes. The place of a whip, about the length of a meter, in Paradise is better than the world and all that is in it. So it is indeed "dunya."

Therefore, when a person dies while a believer, may Allah make us and you among them, and he is carried from the house he lives in and shelters in, where his family, wealth, and dependents are, when his soul departs it says: "Hasten me, hasten me!" Why? Because what it is going to is better than what it is leaving. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿But you prefer the worldly life, while the Hereafter is better and more enduring﴾ [Al-A'la 16-17]. The Hereafter is better and more enduring, but for whom? ﴿And the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah﴾ [An-Nisa 77]. But it is evil for those who do not fear Allah.

It is mentioned that Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, may Allah have mercy on him, who was chief judge in Egypt, once passed by in his procession on a carriage drawn by mules, surrounded by soldiers, and came upon a Jewish oil seller whose clothes were stained with oil and who was struggling to earn a living. The Jew stopped the procession, and said to Ibn Hajar: "Your Prophet claims that «the world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever» [Reported by Muslim (2956) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him]. How does this hadith agree with reality? You are now a believer and he is a Jew, and which of them is more wretched? In this matter the Jew is more wretched. How then does it agree with reality?" Ibn Hajar said: "Yes. What I am in now, compared to the Hereafter, is a prison, because the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah. And what you are in, compared to the Hereafter, is a paradise, because in the Hereafter you will have nothing but the Fire, and what an evil resting place." The Jew said: "I testify that there is no god but Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." Notice how Allah opened this for him, as the truthfulness of the Messenger's words became manifest with complete ease.

The point is that the Hereafter is better than the world and all that is in it. This is why Allah condemned the one who turns away from the remembrance of Allah and desires nothing but the worldly life. Let us ask: does the one who desires the worldly life obtain it?

No, he does not obtain it in full. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Whoever desires the hastening (world), We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We intend. Then We have made Hell for him, which he will enter, blameworthy and expelled﴾ [Al-Isra 18]. It is not what he wills; it is what We will, for whom We intend. ﴿And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it with the striving due to it while he is a believer, those are whose striving is appreciated﴾ [Al-Isra 18-19]. Allah the Exalted also says: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him of it, but he has no share in the Hereafter﴾ [Ash-Shura 20]. The first gets both the worldly and the Hereafter; the second is given part of it, not all of it, and has no share in the Hereafter.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 53, verse 30:**

﴿That is the extent of their knowledge﴾ [An-Najm 53:30]. That is, ﴿that﴾ refers to what is indicated: their being those who turn away and turn their backs, wanting nothing but the life of this world. That is, this is the limit that their knowledge reaches, because their knowledge is deficient. They do not look toward the future, nor do they believe in news (of the unseen). So you will find that their greatest concern is to set right their situation in this world, while turning away from their state in the Hereafter: ﴿That is the extent of their knowledge﴾ [An-Najm 53:30]. And in the transmitted supplication: "O Allah, do not make the world our greatest concern, nor the extent of our knowledge."[[Narrated by at-Tirmidhi (3502) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, and its wording is: "Do not make the world our greatest concern, nor the extent of our knowledge."]]

Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is guided﴾ [An-Najm 53:30]. He, Mighty and Majestic, is most knowing of who has actually strayed from His way and of who will stray. This is because He knows what has been and what will be. His saying ﴿who has strayed﴾ does not mean that He only knows those in whom straying has already occurred; rather, He knows those in whom straying has occurred and those in whom it will occur, because Allah, glorified and exalted, is described with complete knowledge in the present, the future, and the past. His saying ﴿and He is most knowing of who is guided﴾ [An-Najm 53:30] is the opposite of straying. People are between two groups: either one who is guided or one who is astray. Allah, glorified and exalted, only clarified that He is ﴿most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is guided﴾ for two benefits.

The first benefit: that we know that whatever straying and guidance occur, they proceed from Allah's knowledge and by His will, since it is impossible for anything to exist in His creation contrary to what He knows. If it were supposed that something could exist in His creation contrary to what He knows, Allah would be ignorant, and He is far above that.

The second benefit: warning against straying and encouraging guidance. As long as a person knows that any deed that proceeds from him is known to Allah, he will fear disobeying Allah and will be eager to please Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So the benefit is twofold. The first is encouragement toward guidance and the seeking of guidance, and warning against straying. That is, it is as if He is saying: If you go astray, Allah knows you, and if you are guided, Allah knows you, and He will recompense those who did evil according to what they did, and recompense those who did good with the best (reward). ﴿Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is guided﴾ [An-Najm 53:30].

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ [An-Najm 31]. The scholars of rhetoric (balaghah) say: when something that ought to be delayed is brought forward, this indicates restriction and exclusivity (al-hasr wa al-takhsis). Let us examine this verse: is there any delaying and bringing forward in it? ﴿Lillahi ma fi as-samawati wa ma fi al-ard﴾: (lillahi) here is the predicate brought forward (khabar muqaddam), and ﴿ma fi as-samawati﴾ is the delayed subject (mubtada' mu'akhkhar).

So in it, the predicate, which ought to be delayed, has been brought forward. The rule is that the predicate should come after the subject. You say: "al-rajulu qa'imun" (the man is standing), and you do not say: "qa'imun al-rajulu." The original order is that the subject (mubtada') comes first and the predicate (khabar) second, but sometimes the predicate is brought forward for a purpose. Here the purpose is restriction (al-hasr), brothers. Restriction means: it belongs to Allah and not to anyone else. ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ — and no one possesses what is in the heavens and what is on the earth except Allah, blessed and exalted. We possess what we possess of our wealth, but is our ownership comprehensive? It is not comprehensive. My bag is not your bag, and your bag is not my bag. Our possessions are not universal. Then, do we have the right to dispose of what is ours however we wish? No. Our disposal is limited by the Sharia. For this reason, if two people agree to a riba transaction, we say: you two do not own that. If a person wants to burn his wealth, we say: this is forbidden.

Thus the ownership of other than Allah is deficient and not all-encompassing, and the ownership of other than Allah is deficient even in disposal. One of us does not have the right to dispose of his wealth as he wishes, because our disposal of wealth is limited by what the Sharia has brought.

So, who possesses complete, vast, and all-encompassing ownership? Allah, mighty and majestic. For this reason He said: ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ [Ash-Shura 49]. He owns their very essences, and He owns what is in them as well. How many creatures are in the heavens? How many creatures are on the earth? All of it is the property of Allah, mighty and majestic, Who disposes of it as He wills, according to what His wisdom requires. Our belief in this, brothers, that Allah possesses the heavens and the earth, also yields two great benefits:

The first benefit: contentment with Allah's decree. If Allah, mighty and majestic, decrees illness upon you, do not object; if He decrees poverty upon you, do not object. Why? Because you are His property, and He disposes of you as He wills. He disposes of the clouds: He sends rain or withholds it, He causes things to proceed or not to proceed; He disposes of the sun and the moon, He disposes of the creatures, and He disposes of you as well as He wills. If He wills, He gives you health, and if He wills, He takes it away; if He wills, He gives you intellect, and if He wills, He takes it from you; if He wills, He gives you wealth, and if He wills, He takes it from you. You are His property, so when you believe in this, you are content with His decree.

Likewise, the second benefit: contentment with His law, accepting His law and acting upon it, because you are His property. He tells you: do this, do this; He says: do not do this, do not do this. Do you think that if you had a slave and you commanded him but he did not do it, your mastery over him would be complete? No. Or if you forbade him and he did it, your mastery would be deficient.

So if you disobey your Lord, either by committing a prohibited act or by abandoning an obligatory one, you have departed from the requirement of complete servitude, because the requirement of complete servitude is that you submit to His law just as you submit, willingly or unwillingly, to His decree and His destiny. The meaning of His saying, ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ [Ash-Shura 49], is not merely that He informs us that He is the owner. Rather, it is so that we believe in what this ownership requires. And what does it require? Contentment with His decree and contentment with His law. This is the reality of ownership.

﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, that He may recompense those who did evil with what they did and recompense those who did good with the best﴾ [An-Najm 31]. Notice that He used the particle of purpose, ﴿li-yajziya﴾ (that He may recompense). It is as if a speaker says: once it has become clear that ownership belongs to Allah, mighty and majestic, what is the result? The result is that people are divided between the doer of good and the doer of evil, as He, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿He it is who created you, and among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾ [At-Taghabun 2]. If people are divided between the doer of good and the doer of evil, what is the recompense of each one? ﴿That He may recompense those who did evil with what they did﴾ [An-Najm 31]. ﴿Those who did evil﴾ are those who opposed what was commanded or committed what was forbidden; this is the criterion. Those who did evil, they did evil so that He may recompense them with what they did: an evil deed is repaid with an evil deed and no more, or the Mighty and Majestic may pardon whoever deserves pardon, and whoever dies without associating partners with Allah is deserving of pardon: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [An-Nisa' 48]. The point is that it is not possible for Him to add an evil deed that the person did not commit. For this reason He said: ﴿That He may recompense those who did evil with what they did﴾ [An-Najm 31], without increase. ﴿And that He may recompense those who did good with the best﴾ [An-Najm 31]; He did not say "with what they did," because the bounty of Allah is wider than our deeds. ﴿And He recompenses those who did good with the best﴾ [An-Najm 31]: when you do a good deed, it becomes ten good deeds, up to seven hundred times, up to many multiples.

Now consider a close example. The noon prayer (salat al-zuhr) is due in thirty hours, for instance. When you perform wudu' and complete it thoroughly, then go out to the prayer, and nothing takes you out of your house except the prayer, what fruits do you obtain? Every step you take, Allah raises you a degree by it and removes a sin from you by it. How many are your steps? None can count them but Allah, mighty and majestic. Although the intended matter is one thing, which is the prayer, your striving toward the prayer carries a reward. As long as you left your house with nothing taking you out except the prayer, and you prepared in your house, completing the wudu' in your house, you do not take a single step except that Allah raises you a degree by it and removes a sin from you by it. Count your steps: none can count them but Allah.

Then when you reach the mosque and pray as much as Allah wills, then wait for the prayer, and even if the imam's arrival is delayed and the congregational prayer is delayed, the reward of one who prays is written for you: "He remains in prayer as long as he is waiting for the prayer."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (647) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The prayer of a man in congregation is multiplied twenty-five times over his prayer in his house and in his market," and in it: "Let none of you cease to be in prayer as long as he is waiting for the prayer."]] Is this not better than our deeds? Indeed it is. For this reason He said: ﴿And He recompenses those who did good with the best﴾ [An-Najm 31], meaning: with what is better and greater than their deeds. This shows you the vastness of Allah's bounty and His beneficence, and the perfection of His justice. The evildoers He recompenses with justice or pardons, and the good-doers He recompenses with bounty.

Then He mentioned some of their attributes, saying: ﴿Those who avoid major sins and immoralities, except for minor faults﴾ [al-Najm 32]. ﴿Those who avoid﴾ means they keep away from them. Avoidance is called ijtinab (avoiding) because a person stands on one side while the thing he keeps away from stands on another side. So they keep away and do not get involved with major sins (kaba'ir al-ithm) and immoralities (fawahish), ﴿except for minor faults (al-lamam)﴾. ﴿Major sins (kaba'ir al-ithm)﴾ means the major sin (al-kabirah); kaba'ir is the plural of kabirah. Some scholars counted them, and some scholars defined them, and the correct position is definition, meaning that they are bounded by a definition and not merely enumerated. Those who listed them by counting, the apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is that they intended examples. For instance, if a person says they are: associating partners with Allah, sorcery, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden except with right, fleeeing on the day of battle, slandering chaste believing women, consuming usury, and consuming the property of orphans, these are seven. If a person says, "These are the major sins," his statement does not mean that they are limited to this list, since it is possible to understand his words as being merely by way of example.

As for those who defined them, meaning they set a criterion for them (they did not count one, two, three, four, no, a criterion), they said regarding its criterion: every sin for which Allah has prescribed a curse, or wrath, or anger, or disavowal, or the like, is a major sin. I have seen that some of them, among them Shaykh al-Islam (may Allah have mercy on him), said: every sin for which a specific punishment has been prescribed, either in this world or in the Hereafter, is a major sin. On this basis, fornication has a punishment, which is flogging or stoning; theft is a major sin; highway robbery is a major sin; disobedience to parents is a major sin; and so on. Whenever you see a sin for which the Lawgiver has prescribed a specific punishment, it is a major sin.

As for a sin which is only forbidden without any mention of a specific punishment, it is a minor sin, such as a man looking at a non-mahram woman with desire. This is not a major sin; it is one of the minor sins. However, if a person persists in it and it becomes his habit, it becomes a major sin by persistence, not by the act itself. Speaking with a woman in a manner of pleasure is forbidden and is not a major sin. But if a person persists in it, and his only concern becomes calling these women on the phone and talking to them, it becomes a major sin. Thus persistence in a minor sin makes it a major sin in terms of persistence, because his persistence in a minor sin indicates his negligence toward Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and that he is unconcerned with what Allah has forbidden.

So, the major sins (kaba'ir al-ithm) are: every sin for which the Lawgiver has prescribed a specific punishment, either in this world or in the Hereafter. As for what He has forbidden and remained silent about, without mentioning a specific punishment, falling under the general ruling, this is a minor sin; but minor sins, if one persists in them, become major sins through persistence.

His saying: ﴿and immoralities (fawahish)﴾: these are the greatest of the major sins, because among the major sins some are foul (fahish), which are considered very ugly, greatly abhorred, and severely detestable, and some are less than that. For example, fornication is an immorality: ﴿And do not approach fornication; indeed, it is an immorality﴾ [al-Isra' 32]. Sodomy is a greater immorality than fornication, because Allah said regarding fornication: ﴿And do not approach fornication; indeed, it is an immorality﴾ [al-Isra' 32], and He said regarding sodomy, when Lut said to his people: ﴿Do you commit the immorality (al-fahishah)﴾ [al-A'raf 80], using the definite article (al-) which indicates ugliness and that it encompasses all kinds of immoralities.

Marrying within the prohibited degrees is an immorality. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women, except what has already occurred. Indeed, it was an immorality and hatred and an evil way﴾ [al-Nisa' 22]. It is worse than fornication; that is, if a person commits fornication with a non-mahram woman, or with his wife's mother for example, the second is greater, more severe, and more shameful. For this reason, the preponderant view among the scholars is that whoever commits fornication with a woman within his prohibited degrees, even if he is not married (muhsan), shall be stoned. That is, for fornication with women within the prohibited degrees there is no flogging, only stoning, because Allah distinguished between fornication and marrying women within the prohibited degrees. He described marrying within the prohibited degrees with two attributes: ﴿Indeed, it was an immorality and hatred﴾ [al-Nisa' 22], while fornication He described with one: ﴿Indeed, it was an immorality﴾ [al-Isra' 32].

The Sunnah has also distinguished between them, that is, between one who commits fornication with a woman within his prohibited degrees and one who commits it with a non-mahram woman. It made the penalty for the former killing in every case, even if he is unmarried, and even if he is not a thayyib (previously married), because this is greater, may Allah protect us, than a man who commits fornication with his mother, his sister, his wife's mother, or the daughter of his wife with whom he has consummated the marriage. It is a great immorality.

So, ﴿they avoid major sins and immoralities﴾. We have said: the immoralities are the major sins of the major sins, greater.

Can we derive from this verse that major sins differ and immoralities differ? Yes, we derive from the verse that they differ, because "kaba'ir" is a description: the greater it is, the more severe the major sin. The same applies to the immoralities. For this reason, you have heard: ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women, except what has already occurred. Indeed, it was an immorality and hatred﴾ [al-Nisa' 22]; ﴿And do not approach fornication; indeed, it is an immorality﴾ [al-Isra' 32]; ﴿Do you commit the immorality which no one in the worlds preceded you in?﴾ [al-A'raf 80]. Allah distinguished between them, although they are all immoralities, but some of them are greater than others.

﴿Except for minor faults (al-lamam)﴾ [al-Najm 32]. Regarding His saying ﴿except for minor faults﴾, it has been said that it is an exceptive particle connected (istithna' muttasil), and it has been said that it is disconnected (istithna' munqati'), because al-lamam means a small amount. Is the meaning: except a small amount of major sins, meaning they commit a small amount of major sins; or the meaning of ﴿except for minor faults﴾: except minor sins? If we say the first, the exception is connected; if we say the second, the exception is disconnected, and the particle ﴿illa﴾ means "but." The second meaning is closer in terms of division, because Allah mentioned major sins, immoralities, and minor sins. On this basis, the meaning of ﴿except for minor faults﴾ is: except that these righteous people do commit minor sins. Minor sins are, praise be to Allah, expiated by good deeds. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds﴾ [al-Nisa' 31]. The Prophet (ﷺ) informed that: "The five prayers, and Friday to Friday, and Ramadan to Ramadan, are expiation for what is between them, if major sins are avoided." [Narrated by Muslim (233/16) from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "The five prayers, and Friday to Friday, and Ramadan to Ramadan, are expiations for what is between them, if the major sins are avoided."] He (ﷺ) also said: "The 'umrah to 'umrah is an expiation for what is between them." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1773) and Muslim (1349/437) from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him).] On this basis, the meaning is that minor sins fall as expiated either by avoiding major sins, or by avoiding major sins combined with performing these great good deeds: the five prayers, Friday to Friday, Ramadan to Ramadan.

In summary: a person is forgiven for minor sins if he avoids major sins, and if he does good in the five prayers, Friday, and Ramadan.

﴿Indeed, your Lord is vast in forgiveness﴾ [al-Najm 32]. In this sentence there is an allusion to His saying ﴿except for minor faults﴾, meaning that minor faults fall within the vastness of Allah's forgiveness, the Mighty and Majestic, so Allah forgives them. Forgiveness (maghfirah) is the covering of a sin together with overlooking it. Allah covers the sin for you and overlooks it; covering the sin alone is not sufficient, there must be overlooking. The evidence for this is two-fold: linguistic and textual. The linguistic evidence: forgiveness (maghfirah) is derived from maghfar, which is what is placed on the head during battle, called khawdhah, and also called bayd'ah. It is placed on the head to protect against arrows. This which is placed on the head combines two things: protection and covering. Therefore forgiveness requires both covering and protection.

The textual evidence: it is the statement of the Blessed and Exalted: when He is alone with His believing servant on the Day of Resurrection, confronts him with his sins, and he acknowledges them, He says: "I covered them for you in this world, and I forgive them for you today." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2441) and Muslim (2768/52) from Ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both).] This shows that protection from sins and not being held to account for them is part of forgiveness.

﴿Indeed, your Lord is vast in forgiveness﴾ [al-Najm 32]. It was mentioned earlier that ﴿except for minor faults﴾ has two meanings. The first: except minor faults, meaning minor sins; this is one. The second: a small amount of major sins and immoralities, meaning "except a small amount." We mentioned that, based on the difference of the two views, there is disagreement over whether ﴿illa﴾ is connected or disconnected. When is ﴿illa al-lamam﴾ disconnected? When we interpret al-lamam as minor sins, the exception becomes disconnected. The mark of a disconnected exception is that what follows it is not of the same kind as what precedes it. So, for example, in ﴿major sins and immoralities, except for minor faults﴾ [al-Najm 32], if we say al-lamam means minor sins, are minor sins part of major sins and immoralities? No. If we say that al-lamam means a small amount of major sins and immoralities, then "illa" is connected, because a small amount of it is of the same kind as what was previously mentioned. So our exception may be disconnected or connected. What is the connected exception?

If the excepted item is of the same kind as the item from which it is excepted, the exception is connected; if it is not of the same kind, it is disconnected. Consider what the grammarians exemplified. They say: if you say, "The people came except their leader," is the exception connected?

* Student: Connected.
* The Shaykh: Why? Because the leader is of the same kind, one of them.

And they said: if you say, "The people came except a donkey," the exception is disconnected, because a donkey is not of the same kind as the people.

Then He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is vast in forgiveness﴾ [al-Najm 32], pointing to the fact that these are minor sins. It is established in the noble Qur'an that minor sins are forgiven by avoiding major sins. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to an honourable entrance﴾ [al-Nisa' 31]. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is vast in forgiveness﴾.

If we say that al-lamam means a small amount of immoralities and major sins, then His saying ﴿Indeed, your Lord is vast in forgiveness﴾ points to the fact that when a person repents from major sins, Allah forgives him and it is as if they had not been. If he does not repent from them, he is under the will of Allah: if Allah wills, He forgives him, and if He wills, He punishes him in accordance with what this major sin deserves.

Among this Ummah there are people who say that major sins are not forgiven. Who are they? The Kharijites and the Mu'tazilites. Observe: the Kharijites and the Mu'tazilites say that a person who commits fornication is then among the people of the Fire as a disbeliever; likewise if he steals, likewise if he drinks wine. But their statement is false. The correct position is that the doer of a major sin falls under the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [al-Nisa' 48].

If someone says: "If you say this, you have opened the door wide to committing major sins, because any person who commits a major sin will say: perhaps Allah will forgive me." This is indeed a proof used by common people: they say, "If Allah says, ﴿but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾," meaning what is less than shirk for whom He wills, then they will commit major sins and say, "Allah will forgive me." How do you answer this? We answer that Allah said: ﴿He forgives what is less than that﴾, He did not say "for everyone," He said ﴿for whom He wills﴾. Are you now certain that you are among those whom Allah wills to forgive? Does anyone feel certain of this? No one is certain. Therefore, there is no proof in it for the people of disobedience.

Furthermore, His saying ﴿for whom He wills﴾: we know that Allah is All-Wise, and He does not will to forgive a sinner other than for shirk except when wisdom requires it. Which of us can say that Allah's wisdom requires that He forgive me? No one says this. Rather, if one said this, we would say: your statement is itself one of the causes of being held to account and punished, because you have presumed upon Allah.

Then He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿He knows you best, since He produced you from the earth﴾ [al-Najm 32]: He knows us better than that long distant time, ﴿since He produced you from the earth﴾. By what? By the creation of our father Adam, since Adam was created from dust, then became clay, then became dried clay (salsal), then Allah created him with His own hand as a body and breathed into him the spirit, and he became a human being. This is ﴿since He produced you from the earth﴾, the first production.

So we are from the earth. Glory be to Allah, are we from the earth? Yes, we are from the earth: ﴿From it We created you, into it We will return you, and from it We will bring you out a second time﴾ [Ta-Ha 55]. The bringing out after which there is no death, on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿Since He produced you from the earth﴾. For this reason, the children of Adam are now just like the earth: among them are hard, firm soil, among them are soft soil, and among them is what lies between these; among them are white, among them red, among them black, because lands differ in this way. It is mentioned that when Allah wished to create Adam, He took from all the earth: its soft and hard parts, its black and white, and all of it.

﴿And when you were embryos in the wombs of your mothers﴾ [al-Najm 32]. This is the second production. Ajinnah is the plural of janin, which is the fetus, and the fetus is called janin because it is hidden (mustatir). ﴿And when you were embryos﴾ means hidden in the wombs of your mothers. From when to when? From the time a person was a drop (nutfah), from which he is created. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Then We made him a drop in a firm place﴾ [al-Mu'minun 13]. From the time he is a drop, he becomes a fetus, and then he develops through how many stages? Four.

First: a drop, then a clinging clot ('alaqah), then a lump of flesh (mudghah), formed and unformed, then We produced him as another creation: the final stage, in which the soul is placed.

So He knows us in our first production and in our second production in the wombs of our mothers.

﴿So do not justify yourselves﴾ [al-Najm 32]: do not praise yourselves, saying: I did such and such, I prayed, paid zakat, fasted, struggled, performed Hajj. Do not say this; boasting of your deeds before your Lord is not permissible. If someone says: Does not Allah say, ﴿He has succeeded who purifies it﴾ [al-Shams 9]? The answer: yes, but the meaning of ﴿who purifies it﴾ is: whoever does an action by which his soul is purified. The meaning is not "whoever is praised for having done such deeds," but rather it means he did a deed by which his soul is purified. So there is no contradiction between the two verses. For this reason we say: whoever purifies himself by mentioning the good deeds he did has not truly purified himself; whoever purifies himself has not purified himself. There is a difference between them: the self-purification for which a person is praised is that he does a righteous deed by which his soul is purified.

The self-purification for which a person is blamed is that he boasts of his deeds before his Lord and praises himself, as if he were bestowing a favour upon Allah, saying: I prayed, I gave charity, I fasted, I performed Hajj, I struggled, I was dutiful to my parents, and the like. It is not permissible for a person to purify himself by saying: I am such-and-such.

This is a refutation of those Sufis who claim to be imams and purify themselves, and say: we have reached a level where the acts of worship are no longer obligatory for us. There are people now who say that he has reached the world of the divine kingdom (malakut) and there is no prayer upon him, no charity upon him, no fasting upon him, and nothing is forbidden to him. These people have completely departed from religion. Therefore we say: those who purify themselves are the furthest of people from purity, because they have become conceited about their deeds, boasted of them before Allah the Exalted, and assigned to themselves a position which Allah did not assign to them.

﴿So do not justify yourselves; He knows best who is pious﴾ [al-Najm 32]. It is as if He says: why do you purify yourselves? Do you want to inform Allah about what you are doing? The answer: no. For this reason He said: ﴿He knows best who is pious﴾, meaning: if you are conscious of Allah, Allah knows you; there is no need for you to say to Allah, "I did this and that."

This indicates that pronouncing the intention when performing an act of worship may involve a kind of self-purification (tazkiyah). That is, if you want to perform ablution, do you say, "O Allah, I intend to perform ablution"? No. Do you say it silently? No. Some scholars say: say it silently, between yourself and yourself. They gave a reason: so that the tongue matches the heart. The heart has intended, but say with the tongue: "O Allah, I intend to perform ablution." If you intend to pray, also say: "O Allah, I intend to pray." When? Noon or afternoon? Specify: noon. Do you need to state the number of rak'ahs or not? No, you do not need to state a number. Since you have specified it, that is sufficient. Some scholars say this, brothers, eminent jurists.

As for the reason, why pronounce it with the tongue? To make the verbal and the inward intention agree. It is said: this is wrong. This is analogy (qiyas) set against the explicit text. Did the Messenger (ﷺ) prescribe for his community that they pronounce the intention? Never. There is no hadith, neither sound nor weak, that a person, when he wants to act, should pronounce the intention. Never; it does not exist.

Among the amusing anecdotes: a layman in the Sacred Mosque heard a person who wanted to pray. After the iqamah had been called, he said: "O Allah, I intend to pray noon, four rak'ahs, in the Sacred Mosque." When he was about to say the takbir, the man said to him: "You still have something left." He said: "What is left?" He said: "The date. Say: on such-and-such day, of such-and-such month, of such-and-such year. You have now mentioned the place and mentioned the act; the date remains. Say: on such-and-such day of such-and-such month of such-and-such year."

* Student: As an follower (ma'mum)?

* The Shaykh: I do not know whether he was a follower or not. The point is that he said these words to him, and the man came to his senses and said to him: "Brother, you are informing your Lord of your intention? Allah knows your intention: ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal﴾ [Ghafir 19]. There is no need."

Likewise with fasting, for example: when a person eats the pre-dawn meal (suhur) and wants to fast, does he say: "O Allah, I intend the fast until night"? He does not say this. When we were young, they used to teach us this: say, when you have eaten suhur, "O Allah, I intend the fast until night," and we would say it, because we did not know. But in reality, this is among the innovations (bid'ah).

It remains to be said regarding Hajj: do you say, "O Allah, I intend 'umrah," or "I intend Hajj," or "I intend qiran (combined Hajj and 'umrah)," or "tamattu' (the enjoined form)"? No, you do not say it. Even in Hajj, when you bathe and put on the ihram garments, do not say, "O Allah, I intend 'umrah" or "I intend Hajj." The talbiyah suffices, because you will say: "Here I am, O Allah, for 'umrah," if you are performing 'umrah; or "Here I am for Hajj," if you are performing Hajj; or "Here I am for 'umrah and Hajj," if you are performing qiran. So there is no need. All acts of worship are not to be accompanied by pronouncing the intention. For this reason the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿He knows best who has feared Allah﴾ [An-Najm 32].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 53, verses 33–35:

Then Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Have you seen the one who turns away, and gives a little and then withholds? Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so that he sees?﴾ and so on to the end of the verses [An-Najm: 33, 35]. ﴿Have you seen﴾ means: tell me. Wherever "a'ara'ayta" (have you seen) occurs in the Qur'an, it means "tell me." ﴿Have you seen the one who turns away﴾ means: tell me about him, ﴿who turns away﴾, meaning he turns away from obedience to Allah, from faith in Allah and His Messenger, and from establishing the rites of Islam. ﴿And gives a little﴾ means he gives a little wealth. ﴿And then withholds﴾ means he holds back. The meaning is that he is not obedient to Allah, and he is not beneficial to the servants of Allah. He turns away from the obedience of Allah and withholds the bounty of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Therefore Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, questions him, saying: tell me about this. This asking is not because He lacks knowledge, may He be exalted, but to rouse souls and resolves to listen to what is being presented. Then He says: ﴿Have you seen the one who turns away, and gives a little and then withholds? Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so that he sees?﴾ The answer is: No, he does not have knowledge of the unseen. He claims that by his turning away and giving a little he has been safe and saved, but he has not been safe and has not been saved, and he has no knowledge of the unseen that he has been shown.

Then He said: ﴿Or has he not been informed of what is in the scrolls of Moses (36) and of Abraham who fulfilled [his covenant]?﴾ [An-Najm 36, 37] That is: has he not been told what is in the scrolls of Moses? Likewise, [has he not been told about] Abraham ﴿who fulfilled﴾, meaning who fulfilled what Allah commanded him, as in His saying: ﴿And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with certain words, and he fulfilled them﴾ [Al-Baqarah 124]. The meaning is: does this man, who turned away from obedience to Allah, gave little and withheld much, have knowledge of the unseen, that he will be saved by this, or not? And has the news of what is in the scrolls of Moses and Abraham, peace be upon them, come to him? Moses is mentioned because he is the most excellent of the prophets of the Children of Israel, and Abraham is mentioned because he is the father of the prophets: he is the father of the prophets among the descendants of Ishmael and the father of the prophets among the Children of Israel.

As for His saying ﴿who fulfilled﴾, it means who fulfilled what he was commanded, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with certain words, and he fulfilled them﴾. Here Moses is placed before Abraham, whereas in Surah Al-A'la Abraham is placed before Moses. There is no doubt that Abraham is more deserving of being placed first, because he is earlier in time and higher in rank; but for the sake of the rhyme of the verses (fawasil al-ayat) Moses is placed first. Also, because of the special praise for Abraham, Moses is placed first, and so He said: ﴿and Abraham who fulfilled﴾.

What is in the scrolls of Abraham and Moses? He said: ﴿That no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾ [An-Najm 38]. That is, no soul ﴿bearing﴾ (wazirah), meaning one upon whom sin falls, ﴿shall bear the burden (wizr)﴾, meaning sin, ﴿of another (ukhra)﴾. The meaning is that souls do not carry one another's burdens; the burden falls upon whom? Upon its own doer who deserved to be sinful, and it is impossible for anyone else to bear it.

For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Follow our way, and we will bear your sins"﴾ [Al-'Ankabut 12], meaning: follow our path, and we will carry your sins, that is, the sin will be upon us. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But they will not bear anything of their sins. Indeed, they are liars. And they will surely bear their own burdens and additional burdens along with their burdens﴾ [Al-'Ankabut 12, 13]. There is no contradiction in the verses: His saying ﴿they will not bear anything of their sins﴾ refers to reality, while ﴿they will surely bear their own burdens and additional burdens along with their burdens﴾ [Al-'Ankabut 13] applies because they were the ones who misled people, and whoever misleads a person bears his burden and the burden of whoever acted upon it.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 53, verse 42:

﴿And that to your Lord is the final return.﴾ [An-Najm 53:42] There are two recitations of this verse. The first recitation: opening the hamza, ﴿وَأَنَّ إِلَى رَبِّكَ الْمُنْتَهَى﴾ [An-Najm 42]. The second: breaking the hamza, ﴿﴿وَإنَّ إِلَى رَبِّكَ الْمُنْتَهَى﴾ ﴾. Both are sound, canonical (sab'i) recitations. If a person recites with either of them, it is valid. Indeed, it is better for a person who knows the recitations to recite with this one at times and with that one at other times, but not before a crowd of people and in their hearing, because if the common folk hear you reciting contrary to what they know, mischief will result: either they will say, "This man does not know the Qur'an," or they will come to doubt the Qur'an, since the layman may think that (...). Therefore we advise our brothers whom Allah has granted knowledge of recitation not to recite except with the recitation well known among the common people, so that confusion does not arise. But between yourself and yourself, if you fully comprehend the second recitation, then recite with it at times, because all of it is Sunnah; all of it is the speech of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

If it is with the kasra, ﴿﴿وإِنَّ إِلَى رَبِّكَ الْمُنْتَهَى﴾ ﴾, then this sentence and what follows it is not among the scrolls of Ibrahim and Musa; rather, it is a new, independent statement. If it is with the fatha, ﴿وَأَنَّ إِلَى رَبِّكَ الْمُنْتَهَى﴾, then this sentence and what follows it is among what came in the scrolls of Ibrahim and Musa. In either case, it is the speech of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

﴿وَأَنَّ إِلَى رَبِّكَ الْمُنْتَهَى﴾: in what respect? In the affairs of religion and of the world. So, to Allah is the final recourse in matters of knowledge. When a matter of knowledge becomes unclear to us, where do we end? We end with Allah and His Messenger, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿If you dispute over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger﴾ [An-Nisa 4:59]. The Prophet (ﷺ) does not say anything from himself; rather, it is from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Thus the final recourse is to Allah in judging among people and in judging over people.

﴿إِلَى رَبِّكَ الْمُنْتَهَى﴾ also means the final end of all creatures, because this existing creation will perish and transfer to another creation, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Were We then incapable with the first creation? Rather, they are in doubt about a new creation﴾ [Qaf 50:15]. The final end in this sense is the Day of Resurrection. So, to Allah is the final end: to Allah is the ultimate return. Thus the final end of our conditions, our judgments, and everything that proceeds from us and is upon us is to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

And if to Allah is the final end, then to whom do you complain when harm befalls you? To Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And if you desire benefit, from whom do you seek it? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because to Allah is the final end. How many a person has had the means of provision established for him, only to be deprived of it by another at the last moment? He may occupy himself with building a station, for example, intending to earn his living through it, and if Allah does not will this, the station burns down.

So: none brings you good except Allah, and none averts harm from you except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So make Him your final end in all your affairs.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 53, verse 43:

﴿And that it is He who makes [people] laugh and weep.﴾ [An-Najm: 43]

Is the intended meaning the literal act of laughing, or is the intended meaning its necessary consequence, which is joy? Likewise, regarding abka (﴿and He makes weep﴾): is the intended meaning literal weeping, or is the intended meaning sorrow? If we look at the apparent wording, we say: it is literal laughter, and literal laughter arises only from happiness; and ﴿abka﴾ is literal weeping, and weeping occurs only from sorrow. So Allah, exalted is He, makes [people] laugh in this world and makes them weep, and He makes [people] laugh in the Hereafter and makes them weep.

The disbelievers in this world now laugh at whom? At the Muslims, at the believers: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin: 29]. But this laughter will be followed by weeping on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin: 34]. So the One who makes [people] laugh and weep in this world, and the One who makes [people] laugh and weep in the Hereafter, is Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Therefore: He determines what causes laughter and what causes weeping, and He has brought both matters, which are opposites, so that it may be known thereby that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is over all things capable, and that He is the One able to create opposites.

**Qur'an 53:44:** ﴿And that it is He who causes death and gives life.﴾ He causes death in this world and gives life in this world, and He also causes death in this world and gives life in the Hereafter. ﴿He causes death and gives life.﴾ Now, among mankind, you find this: a soul is breathed into today, so God has given it life; and another has its soul removed from its body, so God has caused it to die; and so on and so forth. He is the One who causes death and gives life. There is also a general death and a general life: He caused the world to die in this world and gives them life in the Hereafter. So He is the One who created death and He is the One who created life, and these two are also opposites: life and death, all of them from God, Mighty and Majestic; because God, Exalted is He, is over all things capable.

And that He created the two mates, the male and the female, (45) from a drop of semen when it is emitted (46).

﴿He created the two mates﴾. The word zawj (زوج) means "kind" or "type" (ṣinf). An example is His saying, ﴿And other [punishments] of its kind, in various kinds﴾ [Sad 58], meaning types. Another is His saying, ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their kindred﴾ [al-Saffat 22]. It does not mean their wives; it means their azwāj, that is, their kinds.

So what is meant by ﴿al-zawjayn﴾ (the two mates)? It means the two kinds: ﴿the male and the female﴾ [al-Najm 45], from one substance, ﴿from a drop of semen﴾, which is the seminal fluid, ﴿when it is emitted﴾ [al-Najm 46], meaning when it is poured out and deposited in the woman's womb. God, may He be exalted, created these two differing kinds in their creation, differing in temperament, differing in intellect, and differing in thought, and He created them from one thing, from a drop. For this reason, God, blessed and exalted is He, said at the end of Surah al-Qiyamah: ﴿Then He made of him the two mates, the male and the female. Is not He able to give life to the dead?﴾ [al-Qiyamah 39–40]?

The answer is: yes. God created the two mates, the male and the female, from one thing, and this shows the perfection of His power, may He be exalted. He created two kinds that differ in every respect. Even in physical strength, a man differs from a woman, and in mental, intellectual and organisational capacity, the male differs from the female. Through this we recognise the error of those people who wish to make women equal to men in works that are specific to men. They are feeble-minded and misguided in their religion. How can we equate two things, or two kinds, that God has differentiated in creation and in rank?

There are rulings that are required of men and not required of women, and rulings that are required of women and not required of men. As for destiny and creation, the matter is clear. But these people, who have not been granted success, whom God has deprived of their reason and weakened in their religion, now try to make women equal to men. This is undoubtedly a mistaken idea, contrary to the fitrah (the natural disposition God instilled in humankind) and contrary to nature, and it is also contrary to the Shari'ah (the divine law).

﴿from a drop of semen when it is emitted﴾ [al-Najm 46]. What is the meaning of tumnā (تُمنى, "it is emitted")? It means it is poured out and spilled into the womb. From the same root comes the name of the place Mina (منى), which is near Makkah. The scholars said: this is because blood is poured out there (yumnā fīhi al-dimā'), since the hadi (sacrificial animal) is slaughtered where? It is slaughtered on the day of Eid at Mina, so blood is spilled there. For this reason the place was named after what happens in it.

Then He said: ﴿And that unto your Lord is the final growth (of creation)﴾ [An-Najm 47]. Unto whom? Unto Allah. In this is evidence that Allah has obligated Himself to resurrect the people, because if people lived and died without being returned, this would be pure futility. We now know that people in this world differ in wealth and poverty, strength and weakness, intelligence and reason, and other things. If creation were only like this, without a return, it would be entirely contrary to wisdom. Rather, there must be a return.

Therefore He said: ﴿And that unto Him is the final growth﴾ . What does "upon" (ʿalā) indicate? For example, if you say, "ʿalayka an tafʿala kadha" (it is upon you to do such-and-such), meaning it is obligatory, then ʿalā indicates obligation. So Allah has obligated Himself to bring creation forth again. There is no barrier to Allah imposing upon Himself whatever He wills, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ [Al-An'am 54], meaning He obligated Himself to mercy.

Likewise, here He said: ﴿And that unto Him is the final growth﴾ [An-Najm 47], meaning: unto Allah. Allah obligated Himself to bring the people forth in another growth for recompense, each according to his deeds. The phrase "the other growth" indicates that there was a growth before it, namely the first growth, which is the beginning of the creation of people from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

In His saying "al-ukhra" (the other/final) there is a great benefit: it points out that the One Able to bring about the first is able to bring about the last, and the final growth is easier than the first, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And He is the One who begins creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ [Ar-Rum 27]. All of it is easy for Him, but ease varies in terms of the thing itself, not in terms of Allah's power. Allah's power does not vary: "Be, and it is," whether the thing is the highest or the lowest.

But with respect to what is made, which of the two is easier? Repetition is easier. But with respect to Allah's power, both are one, because the matter is no more than His saying "Be, and it is."

By this we know that some exegetes—may Allah have mercy on them and pardon them—said regarding His saying: ﴿And that is easier for Him﴾ [Ar-Rum 27] that the meaning is: "and it is easy for Him." This is an error. How could Allah say about Himself "and that is easier for Him" and we say "and it is easy"? Rather, we say: "al-hawn" (ease) has two relations: a relation to the object acted upon, and a relation to the agent. With respect to the agent, both are equal, because each of them comes into being by one word: "Be, and it is."

With respect to the object acted upon, it differs; there is no doubt that the first is more difficult than the second.

So, regarding ﴿the final growth﴾, we have said that the word ﴿al-ukhra﴾ carries a benefit: it points out that the One Able to bring about the last is able to bring about the first all the more so. Then we cited in support of this His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And He is the One who begins creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ [Ar-Rum 27].

And that it is He who enriches and suffices (gives possessions).

This means: Allah, glorified and exalted, is the One who extends provision to whom He wills and decrees it. He is the One who enriches, that is, He enriches whomever He wills of His creation. As for "wa-aqna" (and He grants property), it has been said that its meaning is "impoverished" (afqar), because it stands in contrast to "aghna" (enriched). It has also been said that "aghna" means He grants sufficiency, and "aqna" means He grants what exceeds sufficiency. That is, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has extended provision to His servants: among them are those whom He makes independent of others, and among them are those to whom He gives qunya (aqna), meaning He makes for him a qunya, which is the surplus beyond sufficiency.

As we have mentioned many times, when a word can carry two meanings that are not contradictory and there is no preference of one over the other, it is taken to mean both, because this is more comprehensive in meaning.

So it is Allah who enriches, and it is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, who grants property. These idols, namely al-Lat, al-Uzza and Manat, have no part in this; rather, this belongs to Allah alone, Mighty and Majestic.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 53, verse 49:

﴿And that He is the Lord of Sirius (ash-Shi'ra)﴾ [An-Najm: 49]. He used the separating pronoun (damir al-fasl) for emphasis of the sentence. ﴿Lord of Sirius﴾ means: its Creator, its Owner, and its Administrator. ﴿Ash-Shi'ra﴾ is: the bright star that rises in the intense heat. He specified this star because some of the Arabs used to worship it and venerate it. So Allah, blessed and exalted, made clear that Ash-Shi'ra is among the created things that are under His lordship, so it is not a god and does not deserve to be worshipped.

And that He (Allah, Mighty and Majestic) destroyed the first ʿĀd (٥٠) — ﴿وَأَنَّهُ﴾ means Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, ﴿أَهْلَكَ عَادًا الْأُولَى﴾ [An-Najm 50], and they are the people of Hūd.

"Al-Ūlā" (the first) is a descriptive qualifier that clarifies rather than a restrictive one; meaning, there is no "first ʿĀd" and "second ʿĀd." It is one people, but they are an ancient, earlier ʿĀd, and for this reason He described them as "the first," i.e., the ancient, the earlier, and there is no other ʿĀd.

ʿĀd (ʿĀd): they are the people of Hūd. Allah the Exalted had given them strength, vigor, and severity of force beyond that of any others, to the extent that they said: ﴿Who is mightier than us in strength?﴾ [Fuṣṣilat 15]. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Do they not see that Allah, who created them, is mightier than them in strength? And they were rejecting Our signs.﴾ [Fuṣṣilat 15]. These people took pride in their strength and power, so Allah the Exalted destroyed them by the most subtle of things: He destroyed them with a violent, furious wind. ﴿He subjected it against them for seven nights and eight days, consecutively﴾ [Al-Ḥāqqah 7]. It began after dawn and ended at sunset, so the days were eight and the nights seven. ﴿Seven nights and eight days, consecutively, so you would see the people in it fallen as though they were trunks of hollowed-out palm trees﴾ [Al-Ḥāqqah 7]. It lifts a person up to the peak and then hurls him down onto the ground, so they became like hollowed-out palm trunks, and we seek refuge in Allah; or ﴿trunks of uprooted palm trees﴾ [Al-Qamar 20].

So these people, despite their great force and their great might, were not protected by that from the punishment of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

And Thamud [An-Najm 53:51]: meaning, He destroyed Thamud, so He left none of them remaining. Thamud were the people of al-Hijr, to whom Allah sent Salih, but they denied him. Allah the Exalted had given them strength, and had given them knowledge and skill in building construction. Yet despite that, they did not do what Allah intended for them. The Cry seized them, the earth shook beneath them, and they were found lying prostrate in their homes, and we seek refuge in Allah.

And the people of Noah before them. (Qur'an 53:52)

That is: the people of Noah were destroyed before them, drowned. As Allah the Exalted said in the surah "The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split," speaking of their prophet Noah: ﴿So he called upon his Lord, "I am overpowered, so give victory."﴾ ﴿So We opened the gates of the heaven with water pouring down.﴾ [al-Qamar 10-11] And in another reading: ﴿So We opened﴾, which indicates abundance and the intensity of the opening. ﴿The gates of the heaven with water pouring down﴾ [al-Qamar 11], meaning: descending with force. ﴿And We caused the earth to gush forth with springs﴾ [al-Qamar 12]. The whole earth became springs; meaning there was not a span of it but that it was bubbling, to the extent that the oven (tannur), which is the place of kindling, began to bubble, even though the place of kindling is the farthest thing from moisture. Yet it boiled over, and the whole earth became springs while the sky poured down rain.

﴿And the waters met﴾ [al-Qamar 12], the water of the sky and the water of the earth, ﴿for a matter already decreed﴾ [al-Qamar 12]; meaning: a predetermined matter, fixed without any increase or decrease. Glory be to Allah the Mighty. So the people drowned, until the water reached the peaks of the mountains. It is related that "a woman had with her a child; whenever the water rose, she climbed the mountain, and whenever the water rose, she climbed the mountain, until the water reached the summit of the mountain and reached the woman and rose over her body. She had a child with her, so she carried the child on her hands, lifting him so that he would not drown before her." And there has come in a hadith: "If Allah had shown mercy to anyone, He would have shown mercy to the mother of the child."[[Al-Hakim (3349) narrated from 'A'ishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If Allah had shown mercy to anyone of the people of Noah, He would have shown mercy to the mother of the child." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Noah remained among his people for a thousand years less fifty years, calling them, until at the end of his time he planted a tree. It grew tall and spread in every direction. Then he cut it down and began to make it into a ship. They would pass by and ask him, and he would say: 'I am making it a ship.' They would mock him and say: 'You are making a ship on dry land? How will it sail?' He said: 'You will soon know.' When he finished it, the oven boiled over and the water filled the streets. The mother of the child feared for him, for she loved him with a great love. She went out to the mountain until she reached a gap. When the water reached her, she went up with him until she stood on the mountain. When the water reached her neck, she lifted him with her hand until the water carried her away. So if Allah had shown mercy to any of them, He would have shown mercy to the mother of the child."]] But when the word of Allah is fulfilled, there is no repeller of the decree of Allah. May Allah protect us and you from the painful punishment.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, they were more unjust and more transgressive﴾ [an-Najm 52], the exegetes differed concerning His saying ﴿Indeed, they were more unjust and more transgressive﴾. It was said: the pronoun refers to the people of Noah only. It was also said: it refers to all the nations mentioned by Allah the Mighty and Majestic whom He destroyed.

According to the first view, the meaning is: the people of Noah were more unjust and more transgressive than the people of Thamud and 'Ad. The reason for this is that they displayed arrogance and insolence over a long period, since Noah, peace be upon him, remained among them for a thousand years less fifty years. Allah the Blessed and Exalted says about him: ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed I have invited my people night and day. But my invitation has not increased them except in flight. And indeed, every time I invited them that You might forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears﴾ [Nuh 5, 7], so as not to hear; ﴿and covered themselves with their garments﴾ [Nuh 7], wrapping themselves so as not to see. This indicates the intensity of their aversion to what he called them to, peace be upon him. ﴿And they were arrogant with great arrogance﴾ [Nuh 7], meaning: a great arrogance, so they did not submit to the worship of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. Thus they were more unjust and more transgressive than 'Ad and Thamud.

According to the second view, that the pronoun refers to all these nations, the meaning is: these were more unjust and more transgressive than the Quraysh who denied you, O Muhammad. In this there is consolation for the Messenger ﷺ, that Allah the Exalted destroyed these people although they were more unjust and more transgressive than your people; and the One who destroyed those who came before is able to destroy those who come after. Both meanings are correct: these nations were more unjust and more transgressive than Quraysh, and the people of Noah were more unjust and more transgressive than 'Ad and Thamud.

Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And the overturned cities He threw down﴾ [An-Najm 53]. That is, He brought them down. ﴿The overturned cities﴾ are the towns of the people of Lut. ﴿He threw down﴾ means: He sent down. The exegetes differed concerning His words ﴿He threw down﴾: is the meaning that He hurled them from above to below, on the basis that Allah the Exalted lifted these towns up high and then overturned them; or is the meaning that He ﴿threw them down﴾, that is, He sent stones upon them until they demolished the building, so that the top of the building became its bottom?

The essential point is that Allah the Exalted informed about the people of Lut that Allah threw them down, that is, He brought them down, whether from the sky or by the collapse of the building onto its base.

**(The Qur'an, 53:54–55)**

﴿So there covered them that which covered.﴾ *Ghashshāhā* means *ghaṭṭāhā*, i.e., He covered it. His saying ﴿that which covered﴾ is vague, for the sake of magnifying and emphasizing (*ta'ẓīm wa tafkhīm*). It is like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then there covered them from the sea that which covered them﴾ [Ṭā-Hā 20:78], meaning: something great covered them. Thus vagueness is sometimes intended to express magnitude, awe and grandeur, as in this verse: ﴿So there covered them that which covered (54). Then which of the favours of your Lord would you doubt?﴾ [an-Najm 53:54–55]. The interrogative here is for rebuke (*tawbīkh*). *Tatamārā* means to be in doubt, and *al-ālā'* means the blessings. That is: which of the blessings of Allah do you, O human, doubt? For it is obligatory for a person to acknowledge the blessings of Allah and to thank Allah for them, not to doubt and say, "This is from my effort, this is from such-and-such, this is from such-and-such," as the Arabs used to say, "We were given rain by such-and-such *nawʾ*" (the rising or setting of a star), meaning by the star, forgetting the Creator, may He be Mighty and Majestic.

This is the Prophet ﷺ, the one referred to. "Warner" means one who warns, and the warner (munthir) is one who informs of a matter in a manner that instills fear, because inedhar (warning) is informing with intimidation, while bishara (good tidings) is informing with hope. "This is a warner from the warners of old" (﴿هَذَا نَذِيرٌ مِنَ النُّذُرِ الْأُولَى﴾). He did not say "bringer of good tidings" (bashir) because the context requires only the mention of warning, since Allah speaks from the beginning of the surah to its end about the Quraysh, their denial of the Messenger ﷺ, and their worship of idols. So He says: Muhammad ﷺ is a warner from the warners of old; that is, from among the earlier messengers. The meaning is: just as those who denied the messengers suffered punishment and chastisement, so you, O deniers of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, are about to be struck with chastisement and punishment, because Muhammad ﷺ, like others, is a warner from among the warners. Therefore, whoever denies him will suffer the same as what befell the earlier nations.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 53, verse 57:

﴿The Imminent Event has drawn near.﴾ [An-Najm: 57] That is: the Hour has drawn near. ﴿Al-Azifa﴾ (the Imminent Event): the Resurrection (al-qiyama). "Azafa" means "qaraba" (to draw near), and from it is the saying of the poet:

Departure has drawn near, though our mounts have not yet moved from our saddles, and it is as if it had already happened.

Al-Azifa is the Resurrection, because the Hour is near, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.﴾ [Ash-Shura: 17], and He says in the second verse: ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour will be near.﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 63]. So it is near. What indicates its nearness is that Muhammad (ﷺ) is the Seal of the Messengers, meaning that the matter is near. And although Allah mentions that the matter is near, how much time is there between us and the revelation of the Quran? Fourteen centuries, and we are in the fifteenth. Yet Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: "Indeed, the Hour is near." From this we know that the age of this world is long and far off. But should we accept the words of those who speculate and say: "The past age of the world was such-and-such"? No. We neither believe them nor deny them. Sometimes they say: they have found traces of an animal of such-and-such millions of years, or stones or the like. We neither believe this nor deny it, because they do not know the unseen past; they only measure it by the state of the present, meaning they measure, for example, the age of this trace.
